name: High LDL cholesterol
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> High cholesterol (high LDL). Check question: Has a doctor told you your cholesterol or LDL is high or borderline? Yes, high / Yes, borderline (lifestyle-only mode) / No / Never tested (suggest lipid test from age 18, CSI) / Not sure. Follow-ups: Do you take any medicine for cholesterol? No / Yes / Not sure; Has a doctor given you an LDL goal? (enter it) / No / Not sure; Close family member with early heart attack or stroke, or very high cholesterol? Yes / No / Not sure; optional lab entry (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, non-HDL, triglycerides, Lp(a), test date)

waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; high LDL alone does not change water needs. Drink more in heat, exercise or fever per general rules, and drink plenty of water with isabgol or other fibre supplements. With heart disease, heart failure, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, the app shows only the general range and never pushes a higher target. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose high cholesterol; a blood test reviewed by a doctor is needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping, skipping or changing a statin or any cholesterol medicine or dose. Food changes add to medicines but do not replace them. Follow your doctor.
Your LDL goal depends on your total heart risk and is set by your doctor. Indian goals range from under 100 to 30 mg/dL or lower.
LDL of 190 mg/dL or more, especially with a family history of early heart attack, can be inherited (familial hypercholesterolaemia). See a doctor; family members may need testing.
Red yeast rice contains a statin-like compound; EFSA found no safe intake and severe muscle and liver reactions at doses as low as 3 mg/day. Not recommended.
Plant-sterol fortified foods: not for pregnant or breastfeeding women or children under 5; if you take a cholesterol medicine, ask your doctor first; keep under 3 g/day.
Grapefruit juice can raise blood levels of some statins (especially simvastatin). Ask your doctor or pharmacist.
Emergency: chest pain or pressure spreading to the arm, jaw or back, with sweating or breathlessness, or signs of stroke. Seek emergency care now.
With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice on fluids.

requires_doctor_input is true because high LDL is a cardiovascular risk condition whose goal and medicines only a doctor can set; the app sets only general fat-quality, fibre, cholesterol, sodium, sugar and activity guidance on its own.
